text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London finished the day with pared losses after bouncing slightly from an earlier slide.

The contract slumped to a six-month low of $1,477 a tonne in early afternoon trade after it broke through the closely watched $1,500 support level. At the close, it stood $42 down at $1,505. Traders cited aggressive origin selling and fund long liquidation as reasons for the fall.

Arabica futures in New York posted strong gains led by a surge in the September contract, as speculators and the trade bought heavily on fears of a shortage of exchange certified coffee for delivery against the September contract.

By the close September stood at 169.10 cents/lb, up 10.25 cents on the day. Second position December rose 5.80 cents to 151.75 cents/lb, while the back months closed 2.35 to 3.90 cents higher. The September/December switch, a barometer of nearby availability, rose to 17.35 cents compared with 12.90 cents/lb at the close on Monday.

Traders attributed the buying to a potential lack of certified coffee against the September open position after U.S. trade house Cargill stopped a large amount of coffee certified for delivery against July.
That means that Cargill owns over 65,000 bags of coffee which is the majority or the CSCE's certified stockpile as of July 18 of 86,849 bags.

With little certifiable coffee expected to make its way to the exchange ahead of the autumn harvest of many new crop Latin American coffees, some dealers feared a tightening of certified stocks going into September delivery.
In the near term, traders pegged September resistance at 172.00 cents/lb, while support was seen near 165.00 cents/lb.

FUNDAMENTALS - UNITED STATES - After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported that certified coffee inventories rose by 382 60-kg bags as of July 21, to 87.231 bags. An additional 4,859 bags were pending grading, the exchange said. Of the 2,790 bags graded only 1,941 passed, the CSCE said.

SWEDEN - Coffee imports in March 1997 amounted to 201,186 60-kg bags, up from 198,618 bags imported in March, 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1997 (January/March) up to 515,660 bags.

This was a five percent rise on the tonnage imported in the same period the previous year. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Brazil (165,200 vs 91,100 bags), Colombia (117,800 vs 98,200 bags) and Guatemala (53,300 vs 52,300 bags).

Coffee exports in March 1997 reached 21,086 bags, which brought cumulative exports in the first quarter of 1997 up to 62,823 bags compared to 62,706 bags in 1996. Swedish exports are mostly in the form of roast and ground with the United States (37,800 vs 39,200 bags) and Finland (14,400 vs 11,500 bags) being the main markets.
